story.iWant: helpful context when the rain probability is borderline
story.soThat: I can make an informed decision despite the uncertainty
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Verify CloseCallBadge component exists and functions correctly (AC: 1) - Review existing CloseCallBadge component created in Story 3.4 - Verify component location: `components/CloseCallBadge.tsx` - Confirm component accepts `show` boolean prop - Verify message text: "It's a close call - consider bringing an umbrella just in case" - Confirm component is already imported in AnswerDisplay.tsx - Review TypeScript interface for CloseCallBadgeProps
- Task 2: Verify close call logic in AnswerDisplay for YES answers (AC: 1) - Open `components/AnswerDisplay.tsx` and review YES answer branch - Locate CloseCallBadge rendering in YES branch - Verify conditional rendering: `{closeCall && }` - Confirm closeCall flag comes from API response - Verify placement after rain detail cards - Ensure proper spacing and visual hierarchy
- Task 3: Verify close call logic in AnswerDisplay for NO answers (AC: 1) - Open `components/AnswerDisplay.tsx` and review NO answer branch - Locate CloseCallBadge rendering in NO branch - Verify conditional rendering: `{closeCall && }` - Confirm closeCall flag comes from API response - Verify placement after probability display - Ensure consistent styling with YES answer close call badge
- Task 4: Verify message styling is visually distinct but not alarming (AC: 1) - Review CloseCallBadge component styling - Verify glassmorphic styling pattern (backdrop-blur-md, bg-white/10, border-white/20) - Confirm styling uses subtle info color scheme (not error red) - Verify text is clear and readable (text-sm text-foreground) - Ensure message is accessible with high contrast - Confirm responsive design across mobile/tablet/desktop
- Task 5: Verify close call message does NOT appear outside 40-49% range (AC: 1) - Review backend API contract for closeCall flag logic - Verify closeCall = true only when 40 ≤ probability ≤ 49 - Verify closeCall = false when probability < 40 - Verify closeCall = false when probability ≥ 50 - Confirm conditional rendering in AnswerDisplay respects closeCall flag - Test edge cases: 39%, 40%, 49%, 50% probabilities
- Task 6: Verify accessibility for close call message (AC: 1) - Review CloseCallBadge component for semantic HTML - Verify paragraph tag is used for text content - Confirm message is accessible to screen readers - Verify text contrast meets accessibility standards - Ensure message is programmatically associated with answer display - Note: Component uses basic semantic HTML (no ARIA role currently)
- Task 7: Test close call messaging for YES answers (AC: 1) - Test with location returning YES answer with 40-49% probability - Verify "YES, it will rain" displays with rain details - Verify close call message appears after detail cards - Verify message reads: "It's a close call - consider bringing an umbrella just in case" - Verify message styling is subtle and informative (not alarming) - Test at boundary values: 40%, 45%, 49%
- Task 8: Test close call messaging for NO answers (AC: 1) - Test with location returning NO answer with 40-49% probability - Verify "NO, it won't rain" displays with probability only - Verify close call message appears after probability display - Verify message reads: "It's a close call - consider bringing an umbrella just in case" - Verify message styling matches YES answer close call badge - Test at boundary values: 40%, 45%, 49%
- Task 9: Test close call message does NOT appear when inappropriate (AC: 1) - Test YES answer with <40% probability (should NOT show badge) - Test YES answer with ≥50% probability (should NOT show badge) - Test NO answer with <40% probability (should NOT show badge) - Test NO answer with ≥50% probability (note: NO answers are always <50%) - Verify closeCall flag from API response is respected - Test edge cases: 39%, 50%, 60% probabilities
- Task 10: Validate code quality and testing standards (AC: 1) - Run TypeScript type checking: `npm run type-check` - Run ESLint validation: `npm run lint` - Verify zero TypeScript compilation errors - Verify zero ESLint warnings - Test responsive design at 320px, 768px, 1024px breakpoints - Verify both YES and NO close call scenarios work correctly - Confirm CloseCallBadge component is properly documented with JSDoc comments

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: AC 1: Close Call Message Appears for 40-49% Probability - Given: the rain probability is between 40-49% - When: the answer is displayed (YES or NO) - Then: a close call message is shown: "It's a close call - consider bringing an umbrella just in case" - And: the message is visually distinct but not alarming - And: the message appears for both YES and NO answers in this range - And: the message does not appear outside the 40-49% range - And: the message is accessible to screen readers

constraint.rule: Story 3.6 is a verification and testing story - no new code should be written
constraint.rationale: CloseCallBadge component already created in Story 3.4 and integrated in Stories 3.4 and 3.5. Story 3.6 validates existing implementation.

constraint.rule: CloseCallBadge must be a presentational component with no internal state
constraint.rationale: Single responsibility principle. Component only renders message based on show prop. Parent components (AnswerDisplay) handle conditional logic.

constraint.rule: CloseCallBadge must use glassmorphic styling pattern consistent with DetailCard components
constraint.rationale: Visual consistency across all detail displays. Classes: backdrop-blur-md, bg-white/10, border border-white/20, rounded-lg.

constraint.rule: Close call message must use subtle color scheme (not alarming red)
constraint.rationale: Message indicates uncertainty, not danger. Current implementation uses text-foreground (neutral). Amber color considered but not implemented to maintain simplicity.

constraint.rule: Close call message appears ONLY when closeCall flag is true from API response
constraint.rationale: Backend (Epic 2) owns business logic for 40-49% range. Frontend trusts closeCall flag without recalculating.

constraint.rule: Single CloseCallBadge component used for both YES and NO answers
constraint.rationale: Component reusability. Same message, same styling, same behavior for all close call scenarios.

constraint.rule: Close call message must be accessible to screen readers
constraint.rationale: Semantic HTML (paragraph tag) ensures screen reader compatibility. Text is clear and user-friendly.

constraint.rule: Manual testing only - no automated unit tests in Epic 3
constraint.rationale: Epic 3 test strategy: manual browser testing, TypeScript validation, ESLint checks. Automated tests deferred to Epic 5.

constraint.rule: Story 3.6 assumes backend correctly sets closeCall flag for 40-49% probability
constraint.rationale: Backend logic (Epic 2) already implemented. If backend has bugs, those are Epic 2 issues, not Story 3.6 scope.

interface.name: CloseCallBadgeProps
interface.description: Props for CloseCallBadge component. Single boolean prop controls visibility. When show=false, component returns null (early return pattern).

interface.name: RainCheckResponse.closeCall
interface.description: Backend API response field indicating close call scenario (40-49% probability). Backend sets to true when 40 ≤ probability ≤ 49, false otherwise. Frontend reads flag and conditionally renders CloseCallBadge.

interface.name: AnswerDisplay Integration
interface.description: CloseCallBadge conditionally rendered in AnswerDisplay based on closeCall flag from API response. Pattern used in both YES answer branch (line 107) and NO answer branch (line 129).

tests.standards: Epic 3 testing standards: Manual browser testing on http://localhost:3000. No automated unit tests in Epic 3 (deferred to Epic 5.7). TypeScript type checking via `npm run type-check`. ESLint validation via `npm run lint`. Responsive design testing at 320px, 768px, 1024px breakpoints. Accessibility verification with semantic HTML and screen reader announcements. Edge case testing for boundary probabilities (39%, 40%, 49%, 50%).
tests.locations: - Manual testing: http://localhost:3000 in browser - TypeScript validation: npm run type-check command - ESLint validation: npm run lint command - Responsive testing: Browser DevTools responsive mode - No automated test files in Epic 3

test-idea.scenario: Close call message appears for YES answer with 40-49% probability
test-idea.approach: Configure backend to return YES answer (willRain: true) with probability 45% and closeCall: true. Search location, verify "YES, it will rain" displays with rain details. Verify close call message appears after detail cards: "It's a close call - consider bringing an umbrella just in case". Verify glassmorphic styling is present.

test-idea.scenario: Close call message appears for NO answer with 40-49% probability
test-idea.approach: Configure backend to return NO answer (willRain: false) with probability 45% and closeCall: true. Search location, verify "NO, it won't rain" displays with probability only. Verify close call message appears after probability display. Verify message is identical to YES answer close call message.

test-idea.scenario: Close call message does NOT appear at 39% probability (below threshold)
test-idea.approach: Configure backend to return probability 39% with closeCall: false. Search location, verify answer displays (YES or NO based on threshold). Verify close call message does NOT appear. Verify no rendering artifacts or empty divs.

test-idea.scenario: Close call message appears at 40% probability (lower boundary)
test-idea.approach: Configure backend to return probability 40% with closeCall: true. Search location, verify close call message appears. This validates the lower boundary is inclusive (40 ≤ probability).

test-idea.scenario: Close call message appears at 49% probability (upper boundary)
test-idea.approach: Configure backend to return probability 49% with closeCall: true. Search location, verify close call message appears. This validates the upper boundary is inclusive (probability ≤ 49).

test-idea.scenario: Close call message does NOT appear at 50% probability (above threshold)
test-idea.approach: Configure backend to return probability 50% with closeCall: false. Search location (should be YES answer at 50%). Verify close call message does NOT appear. This validates the upper boundary is exclusive (probability > 49 means no close call).

test-idea.scenario: Close call message styling is visually distinct but not alarming
test-idea.approach: Display close call message and visually inspect styling. Verify glassmorphic effect (backdrop-blur-md, semi-transparent background). Verify border is subtle (border-white/20). Verify text color is neutral (text-foreground, not red/error color). Verify message is readable with good contrast.

test-idea.scenario: Close call message is accessible to screen readers
test-idea.approach: Use browser inspector to verify CloseCallBadge HTML structure. Verify paragraph tag is used (semantic HTML). Check for text content: "It's a close call - consider bringing an umbrella just in case". If screen reader available (VoiceOver, NVDA), verify message is announced when displayed.

test-idea.scenario: Close call message is responsive across device sizes
test-idea.approach: Open browser DevTools responsive mode. Test at 320px (mobile), 768px (tablet), 1024px (desktop). Verify close call message displays correctly at all sizes. Verify text wraps appropriately. Verify no horizontal scrolling. Verify message remains readable without zooming.

Run `npm run type-check` in will-it-rain directory. Verify zero TypeScript errors. Run `npm run lint`. Verify zero ESLint warnings or errors. This validates CloseCallBadge component and AnswerDisplay integration are type-safe and follow code quality standards.
